messages:
sam holland: quick follow-up from the packaging RFC — we need to nail operator retry/grace windows and how compact manifests affect activation timing. link: https://rfc.internal/onprem-packaging

olivia ng: thanks. can you summarize the exact failure we're protecting against? is this mostly about transient disk full / operator restarts, or about long-delayed seed syncs in airgapped setups?

sam holland: both. two concrete cases: 1) operator restarts during apply -> we need deterministic idempotent resume; 2) long tail partial syncs where activation must not deadlock waiting for missing blobs.

raj patel: +1. my proposal: add a short "operator grace period" after manifest activation where nodes accept the new manifest but run activation in background. during grace, traffic is routed to old image unless all required blobs present.

eva kim: that feels safer for customer workloads. how do we detect "all required blobs present" cheaply? can't always fetch whole manifest to check.

sam holland: idea: manifest carries a compact bloom-like summary + counts. operator can check local cache headers and blob index for presence. if summary mismatch we treat as partial and extend the grace window.

olivia ng: sample config snippet for operator policy:

```
activation_grace_seconds: 900  # default 15m
manifest_check_mode: compact-scan | full-verify
partial_threshold_pct: 95
```

what about defaults? 15m seems fine but long airgapped transfers could need hours.

raj patel: allow per-catalog overrides + heuristics: if catalog source==local-registry then grace=24h; if source==online then 15m. also surface a "manual-force-activate" for operators.

eva kim: concern: long grace windows increase risk of running mixed component versions. need a safety cutoff and automatic rollback if critical components missing after X.

sam holland: agree. plan: two windows: grace (soft) and hard-deadline. soft allows background fetches; hard triggers rollback or pause. default hard = 72h for local-registry, 1h for online.

olivia ng: how do we handle the control plane surface? console should show per-node activation state: pending blobs, percent complete, time to hard-deadline. ops-bot can post alerts when node crosses thresholds.

ops-bot: alert configured: channel=#eng-oncall, severity=warning when node_grace_remaining < 20% and < 30 required blobs missing.

raj patel: two more: 1) compact manifests must include per-component compatibility matrix (min-runlevel) so partial applies can't enable features that break old components. 2) signing: include "prune-intent" metadata so operator prunes only once manifest is hard-activated and signed-prune epoch advanced.

sam holland: good call. that prevents accidental blob deletes during long grace. also think we should version the compact summary algorithm and fall back to full-verify if unknown version.

eva kim: operational runbook notes:
- operator sees manifest M1 -> starts activation -> checks compact summary -> partial -> extend grace -> begin background fetch -> if hard deadline reached -> send rollback notice -> hold for manual ack or auto-rollback based on policy.

olivia ng: can we make the fetcher do prioritized blob pull: critical components first, then optional. helps reduce risk of hitting hard-deadline.

sam holland: yep. implement priority tag in manifest, planner fetches critical blobs first. also add a mode: "apply-as-progressive" where routes are shifted gradually to new manifest as criticals come online.

raj patel: one last integration: dedupe with existing seed-sync resume token logic. manifest compact summary should include seed-sync checkpoint id so we can resume fetch without re-checks.

sam holland: next steps: i'll update the RFC with these windows, compact summary fields, and runbook pseudocode. can folks review the draft by EOD tomorrow?

olivia ng: reviewing. sending a few inline questions in the RFC doc. :thumbsup:

eva kim: i'll test the priority fetcher in the local-registry sim and share metrics.

sam holland: thanks all. closing thread when RFC patch lands.
